item.title: Lally AI Academy Applications Now Open
item.description: Have an AI idea you want to bring to life? The Lally AI Academy is a 30-day, hands-on sprint where student teams build and deploy live AI-powered products with a $500 budget, mentorship, and professional-grade tools. No coding background required! Teams must include at least one Lally student. Applications for Cohort 2 close September 15. Apply Today!

item.title: STS Colloquium with Ashley Shew Slated for 9/9
item.description: This talk takes us through the impetus and set up of disability-forward technology consulting. We begin by looking at disabled critiques of technology, trials in setting things up to get disabled feedback, ideas for setting up disability-forward research, and then we discuss real examples of disability consulting sessions set up by Shew through the DisCoTec Center. Come listen on 9/9 at 11:30am in Sage 5711.

item.title: A Control-Theoretic Perspective on Game-Theoretic Learning
item.description: ISE The framework of multi-agent game-theoretic learning explores how individual agent strategies evolve in response to the strategies of others. A central question is whether these evolving strategies converge to classical solution concepts, such as Nash equilibrium. This talk adopts a control-theoretic perspective by recognizing that learning agents interacting with one another form a feedback system. Learning dynamics are modeled as open dynamical systems that map payoffs, regardless of…

item.title: TWed Talk: Sabrina Kirrane on “Law as Code: From Legal Text to Machine Actionable Policies and Norms” (4:00p, 09 Sep, Winslow 1140)
item.description: In this talk Dr. Sabrina Kirrane of the Vienna University of Economics and Business will explore how hybrid NLP techniques tailored for the legal domain are used to automatically extract norms from legal text; and how knowledge graphs and machine actionable policies can be used to encode policies and norms in a manner that facilitates automated compliance and governance. In both cases, she’ll compare and contrast various techniques and highlight open research challenges and opportunities.

item.title: Chris Lirakis & Rucyl Mills on Quantum
item.description: Date: Thursday, September 10, 2026 6:00 PM - 7:00 PM - How might quantum physics help us think about living with uncertainty? For the first Interface talk of the year, artist and composer Rucyl Mills joins physicist and computing pioneer Chris Lirakis for a conversation on how artists and scientists approach things they cannot fully see, predict, or understand. All are welcome. Stay afterwards for refreshments and informal conversation in Evelyn’s Café at EMPAC.
